title: History Lec 2
summary: Buddha: born 563 BC at Lumbini in the Shakya clan; father Suddhodana, mother Mahamaya, wife Yashodhara; Great Renunciation (Mahabhinishkramana) at 29, enlightenment at Bodh Gaya at 35, Mahaparinirvana at Kushinagar.
Symbols: Great Renunciation - horse; Enlightenment - Bodhi tree; First Sermon (Dhammachakra Pravartana, Sarnath) - wheel; Mahaparinirvana - stupa.
Tripitaka (Pali): Sutta (sermons), Vinaya (rules), Abhidhamma (philosophy); the 5 Nikayas of the Sutta Pitaka: Digha, Majjhima, Samyutta, Anguttara, Khuddaka.
Texts: Dhammapada (Gita of Buddhism), Visuddhimagga - Buddhaghosa, Buddhacharita - Ashvaghosha, Milindapanho - Nagasena and Menander, Mahabhashya - Patanjali, Panchatantra - Vishnu Sharma.
Parts of a stupa: Anda, Harmika, Chhatra, Yashti, Medhi/Vedika, Torana, Pradakshina Path; the three chhatras = Triratna (Buddha, Dhamma, Sangha).
Four Buddhist Councils: Rajagriha (483 BC), Vaishali (383 BC), Pataliputra (250 BC), Kundalvana-Kashmir (Kanishka); patrons A-K-A-K, presidents M-S-M-V.
Hinayana (Pali; Sri Lanka, Thailand, Cambodia) and Mahayana (Sanskrit; China, Korea, Japan); Bodhisattvas: Padmapani, Vajrapani, Manjushri.

Jainism: Triratna (Right Knowledge, Right Faith, Right Conduct), five vows (Panchavrata); 45 Agamas, 12 Angas (first Acharanga, last Drishtivada); two councils at Pataliputra (~298 BC) and Vallabhi (512 AD).

Tirthankaras: Rishabhadeva (1st, bull), Arishtanemi (22nd, conch), Parshvanath (23rd, serpent), Mahavira (24th, lion); Mahavira's father Siddhartha, mother Trishala, born at Kundagrama, died at Pavapuri, first disciple Jamali.
Chandragupta Maurya defeated Dhana Nanda in 322 BC; performed Sallekhana at Shravanabelagola with Bhadrabahu; Digambara - Bhadrabahu, Shvetambara - Sthulabhadra; Bindusara followed the Ajivikas.
Mauryan administration: Saptanga theory; Sitadhyaksha, Samaharta, Sannidhata, Nagarika, Gopa, Shulkadhyaksha, Samsthadhyaksha, Rajuka, Yukta, Gramika; taxes: Hiranya, Pranaya, Parshvika, Senabhaktam.
Provinces and capitals: Uttarapatha - Taxila, Avanti - Ujjain, Prachi - Pataliputra, Kalinga - Tosali, Dakshinapatha - Suvarnagiri; silver punch-marked coins.

Ashoka: Kalinga War 261 BC; Dhammaghosha, Dhamma Mahamattas; 14 Major Rock Edicts (13th on Kalinga), 7 Pillar Edicts; language Prakrit, scripts Brahmi, Kharosthi, Greek, Aramaic; deciphered by James Prinsep in 1837.

Sarnath Lion Capital is the National Emblem; Rampurva bull capital in Rashtrapati Bhavan; Nigali Sagar and Rummindei inscriptions in Nepal; Barabar-Nagarjuni caves for the Ajivikas (Ashoka/Dasharatha).
Others: Ajanta - Satavahanas/Vakatakas, Elephanta - Shiva, Bhimbetka - Wakankar, Bagh - Buddhist, Udayagiri-Khandagiri (Odisha) - Kharavela; ports Bharuch, Sopara, Tamralipti.

mcqs.q: At what age did Gautama Buddha attain enlightenment at Bodh Gaya (Bihar)?
mcqs.e: Buddha left home at 29 and attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya at 35.

mcqs.q: Where was Gautama Buddha born?
mcqs.e: He was born at Lumbini around 563 BC.

mcqs.q: In which year is Gautama Buddha traditionally believed to have been born?
mcqs.e: Buddha's birth is traditionally dated to 563 BC.

mcqs.q: To which clan did Gautama Buddha belong?
mcqs.e: Hence he is called Shakyamuni.

mcqs.q: Who were the father and mother of Gautama Buddha respectively?
mcqs.e: Buddha's father was Suddhodana and his mother Mahamaya.

mcqs.q: In Buddhism, what is Buddha's renunciation of home called?
mcqs.e: Buddha undertook the Mahabhinishkramana (Great Renunciation) at the age of 29.

mcqs.q: Which symbol represents Buddha's Great Renunciation (Mahabhinishkramana)?
mcqs.e: The horse (Kanthaka) depicts his departure from home.

mcqs.q: Which symbol represents Buddha's Mahaparinirvana?
mcqs.e: Stupas enshrine the relics of the Buddha.

mcqs.q: What was the name of Buddha's horse?
mcqs.e: His charioteer was Channa.

mcqs.q: Who was Buddha's maternal aunt (foster mother) and the first Buddhist nun?
mcqs.e: Mahaprajapati Gautami became the first nun of the Sangha.

mcqs.q: What was the name of Gautama Buddha's wife?
mcqs.e: Yashoda was the wife of Mahavira.

mcqs.q: Who were the two early teachers of Gautama Buddha?
mcqs.e: Buddha learnt meditation from them.

mcqs.q: Which Buddhist text affirms the doctrine of Anatta by declaring all dhammas to be 'without self'?
mcqs.e: Kalpasutra, Bhagavati Sutra and Uttaradhyayana are Jain texts.

mcqs.q: Which Pitaka contains the rules of conduct and monastic life for Buddhist monks?
mcqs.e: The Vinaya Pitaka contains the rules for monks and nuns.

mcqs.q: In which language is the Tripitaka written?
mcqs.e: All three Pitakas are in Pali, hence called the Pali Canon.

mcqs.q: In which Pitaka are Buddha's sermons compiled?
mcqs.e: Buddha's dialogues and sermons are in the Sutta Pitaka; Ananda was his chief disciple.

mcqs.q: What does the Abhidhamma Pitaka deal with in depth?
o: Philosophical teachings, mental phenomena and psychological insights
mcqs.e: The Abhidhamma contains the philosophy of Buddha's teachings.

mcqs.q: Which text contains stories of the previous births of the Buddha?
mcqs.e: The Jataka tales narrate the Buddha's previous births.

mcqs.q: Who composed the Panchatantra?
mcqs.e: The Panchatantra fables were written by Vishnu Sharma.

mcqs.q: Which text is called the 'Gita of Buddhism'?
mcqs.e: The Dhammapada is called the Gita of Buddhism for its essence of teachings.

mcqs.q: Who is the author of the Visuddhimagga?
mcqs.e: Buddhaghosa was a renowned Pali scholar.

mcqs.q: Who wrote the 'Buddhacharita'?
mcqs.e: Ashvaghosha was a poet in the court of Kanishka.

mcqs.q: 'Milindapanho' is a dialogue between whom?
o: Indo-Greek ruler Menander and Buddhist monk Nagasena
mcqs.e: Milindapanho means 'Questions of Milinda'; Milinda later became a Buddhist.

mcqs.q: Who is the author of the 'Mahabhashya'?
mcqs.e: Patanjali was a contemporary of Pushyamitra Shunga.

mcqs.q: In which Buddhist structure are the relics of the Buddha enshrined?
mcqs.e: Stupas enshrine relics of the Buddha or Bodhisattvas.

mcqs.q: In Buddhist architecture, what is a 'Chaitya'?
mcqs.e: A vihara is the residence of monks.

mcqs.q: What is the residence of Buddhist monks called?
mcqs.e: A chaitya is a prayer hall.

mcqs.q: What is the hemispherical dome of a stupa called?
mcqs.e: The Anda is the main hemispherical part of a stupa.

mcqs.q: What is the gateway of a stupa called?
mcqs.e: The torana is the gateway; the railing is called the vedika.

mcqs.q: What is the circumambulatory path around a stupa called?
mcqs.e: The pradakshina path is enclosed by a railing (vedika).

mcqs.q: What do the three umbrellas (chhatras) on top of a stupa symbolise?
mcqs.e: The Three Jewels of Buddhism are Buddha, Dhamma and Sangha.

mcqs.q: Which stupa marks the place where Buddha delivered his first sermon?
mcqs.e: The first sermon was delivered at the Deer Park (Mrigadava) in Sarnath near Varanasi.

mcqs.q: What is Buddha's first sermon called?
mcqs.e: It means 'turning the wheel of Dhamma' and its symbol is the wheel.

mcqs.q: In which state is the Amaravati Stupa located?
mcqs.e: The Amaravati stupa is known for its white limestone (marble-like) sculptures.

mcqs.q: What symbolises Buddha's enlightenment?
mcqs.e: He attained enlightenment under the Bodhi tree at Bodh Gaya.

mcqs.q: Which caves, famous for paintings and sculptures, are a masterpiece of Buddhist art?
mcqs.e: Elephanta is associated with Shiva, Bhimbetka with the Stone Age.

mcqs.q: Which is the most famous sculpture of the Elephanta Caves?
mcqs.e: The Elephanta caves are dedicated to Lord Shiva.

mcqs.q: Where are the Bhimbetka rock shelters located?
mcqs.e: Discovered by V.S. Wakankar; they belong to the Stone Age.

mcqs.q: Who discovered the Bhimbetka rock shelters?
mcqs.e: Bhimbetka is associated with the Palaeolithic, Mesolithic and Neolithic periods.

mcqs.q: Which dynasties are associated with the construction of the Ajanta Caves?
mcqs.e: The Satavahanas and Vakatakas contributed to the Ajanta caves.

mcqs.q: The Bagh Caves of Madhya Pradesh are associated with which religion?
mcqs.e: The Bagh caves are examples of Buddhist art.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT part of the Triratna of Jainism?
mcqs.e: Jain Triratna: Right Knowledge, Faith and Conduct; Right Livelihood is part of the Eightfold Path.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT among the five vows (Panchavrata) of Jainism?
mcqs.e: The five vows: Ahimsa, Satya, Asteya, Brahmacharya, Aparigraha.

mcqs.q: What does 'Aparigraha' mean in Jainism?
mcqs.e: Aparigraha means not being attached to possessions or persons.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT a principle of Jainism?
o: Belief that even stones and water have life
Rejection of the doctrine of karma
Renunciation as the path to liberation
mcqs.e: Jainism accepts the doctrine of karma; it does not reject it.

mcqs.q: What is the first of the 'Four Noble Truths' of Buddhism?
o: The world is full of suffering
Suffering ends through the Eightfold Path
Desire is the cause of suffering
mcqs.e: The second truth is that desire (tanha) is the root cause of suffering.

mcqs.q: What is the path to end suffering in Buddhism?
mcqs.e: The Eightfold Path includes right speech, action, effort, resolve, view, concentration, livelihood and mindfulness.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT part of the Eightfold Path?
mcqs.e: Aparigraha is one of the Jain five vows.

mcqs.q: Which revered Shvetambara Jain text describes the lives of the 24 Tirthankaras and is read during Paryushana?
mcqs.e: Paryushana is observed for 8-10 days around August-September.

mcqs.q: Paryushana is a major festival of which religion?
mcqs.e: It is celebrated around August-September.

mcqs.q: What are the two sects of Jainism?
mcqs.e: Shvetambaras wear white clothes; Digambaras remain unclothed.

mcqs.q: Which Jain text, well known in the West, deals with monastic conduct, sermons and poetic teachings?
mcqs.e: The Acharanga Sutra, first of the 12 Angas, focuses on monastic conduct.

mcqs.q: How many Agamas are recognised in the Shvetambara tradition?
mcqs.e: There are 45 Agamas, including the 12 Angas.

mcqs.q: Which is the last (12th) of the 12 Angas of Jainism?
mcqs.e: The first is Acharanga and the twelfth is Drishtivada.

mcqs.q: Where was the first systematic compilation of Jain literature (First Jain Council) held?
mcqs.e: The first council was held at Pataliputra around 298 BC, compiling the 12 Angas.

mcqs.q: Where and when was the Second Jain Council held?
mcqs.e: It was presided over by Devardhi Kshamashramana.

mcqs.q: Who presided over the First Jain Council (according to tradition)?
mcqs.e: It was held during the reign of Chandragupta Maurya.

mcqs.q: How many Buddhist Councils were held in all?
mcqs.e: Rajagriha, Vaishali, Pataliputra and Kundalvana (Kashmir).

mcqs.q: What is the correct order of the four Buddhist Councils?
mcqs.e: Order: Rajagriha - Vaishali - Pataliputra - Kundalvana.

mcqs.q: Who were the patrons of the four Buddhist Councils respectively?
mcqs.e: Memory trick: A-K-A-K.

mcqs.q: Who presided over the four Buddhist Councils respectively?
mcqs.e: Memory trick: M-S-M-V.

mcqs.q: Where was the Third Buddhist Council held?
mcqs.e: It was held around 250 BC under Ashoka's patronage.

mcqs.q: In which year was the First Buddhist Council held?
mcqs.e: The Second Council was in 383 BC and the Third in 250 BC.

mcqs.q: Where, and under whose patronage, was the Fourth Buddhist Council held?
mcqs.e: Kanishka was a Kushana ruler; Buddhism split into two sects at this council.

mcqs.q: Into which two sects did Buddhism split at the Fourth Buddhist Council?
mcqs.e: Hinayana means 'Lesser Vehicle' and Mahayana 'Greater Vehicle'.

mcqs.q: In which countries are followers of Hinayana mainly found?
mcqs.e: Their scriptures are in Pali and they do not believe in image worship.

mcqs.q: In which countries did Mahayana mainly spread?
mcqs.e: Their scriptures are in Sanskrit and they practise image worship.

mcqs.q: The concept of the Bodhisattva is associated with which sect?
mcqs.e: A Bodhisattva postpones his own nirvana to help others attain enlightenment.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT a Bodhisattva?
mcqs.e: Padmapani, Vajrapani and Manjushri are famous Mahayana Bodhisattvas.

mcqs.q: Vajrapani is known as the Bodhisattva of what?
mcqs.e: Padmapani is also called Avalokiteshvara.

mcqs.q: Which five Nikayas make up the Sutta Pitaka of the Tripitaka?
mcqs.e: Nikaya means collection.

mcqs.q: What does the Digha Nikaya mean?
mcqs.e: Majjhima = middle-length, Anguttara = numerical, Khuddaka = minor, Samyutta = connected.

mcqs.q: What is the Anguttara Nikaya known for?
mcqs.e: Anguttara = numerical discourses.

mcqs.q: During a famine in Magadha, with whom did Chandragupta Maurya go to Shravanabelagola?
mcqs.e: There he gave up his life through Sallekhana (fasting unto death).

mcqs.q: What is the Jain practice of voluntarily fasting unto death called?
mcqs.e: Sallekhana is also called Santhara.

mcqs.q: In which state is Shravanabelagola located?
mcqs.e: Bhadrabahu and Chandragupta Maurya went there.

mcqs.q: Who is regarded as the leader of the Digambara sect?
mcqs.e: Jains who stayed in Magadha under Sthulabhadra came to be called Shvetambaras.

mcqs.q: Who is regarded as the leader of the Shvetambara sect?
mcqs.e: Shvetambaras wear white clothes.

mcqs.q: Who got the Udayagiri-Khandagiri caves of Odisha excavated?
mcqs.e: They contain carvings of Jain Tirthankaras; another Udayagiri cave group is in Madhya Pradesh.

mcqs.q: Who was the first Tirthankara of Jainism?
mcqs.e: His symbol is the bull (Vrishabha).

mcqs.q: Who was the 23rd Tirthankara of Jainism?
mcqs.e: His symbol is the serpent.

mcqs.q: Who was the 22nd Tirthankara?
mcqs.e: His symbol is the conch.

mcqs.q: Which two Tirthankaras are mentioned in the Vedas?
mcqs.e: Only Rishabhadeva and Arishtanemi find mention in the Vedas.

mcqs.q: What is the symbol of Mahavira?
mcqs.e: Mahavira was the 24th Tirthankara.

mcqs.q: What were the names of Mahavira's father and mother?
mcqs.e: Trishala was a Lichchhavi princess.

mcqs.q: What was the name of Mahavira's wife?
mcqs.e: Yashodhara was the wife of the Buddha.

mcqs.q: What was the name of Mahavira's daughter?
mcqs.e: Her husband Jamali became Mahavira's first disciple.

mcqs.q: Who was the first disciple of Mahavira?
mcqs.e: Jamali was the husband of Mahavira's daughter.

mcqs.q: Where was Mahavira born?
mcqs.e: Mahavira belonged to the Jnatrika clan of the Vajji confederacy near Vaishali.

mcqs.q: Where did Mahavira die?
mcqs.e: Buddha died at Kushinagar.

mcqs.q: Where did Gautama Buddha attain Mahaparinirvana?
mcqs.e: Buddha died at Kushinagar.

mcqs.q: Where did Mahavira attain Kaivalya (supreme knowledge)?
o: Bodh Gaya, under a peepal tree
Jrimbhikagrama, on the bank of the Rijupalika river, under a sal tree
mcqs.e: He attained Kaivalya on the bank of the Rijupalika river.

mcqs.q: What is Mahavira considered to be in Jainism?
o: Its chief propagator, not the founder
mcqs.e: Rishabhadeva is considered the founder of Jainism.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is one commonly cited date range for Mahavira's life?
mcqs.e: Mahavira is dated 540-468 BC (traditional dating: 599-527 BC).

mcqs.q: In which year did Chandragupta Maurya found the Mauryan Empire?
mcqs.e: He defeated Dhana Nanda of the Nanda dynasty.

mcqs.q: Who founded the Nanda dynasty?
mcqs.e: The last Nanda ruler was Dhana Nanda.

mcqs.q: Which Nanda ruler was defeated by Chandragupta Maurya?
mcqs.e: This was achieved with the help of Kautilya (Chanakya).

mcqs.q: By what other names is Kautilya known?
mcqs.e: Kautilya wrote the Arthashastra.

mcqs.q: The Arthashastra is primarily a treatise on which subject?
mcqs.e: It describes how a king should govern the state.

mcqs.q: To whose court did Seleucus send his ambassador Megasthenes?
mcqs.e: The court was at Pataliputra.

mcqs.q: What is the name of Megasthenes' book?
mcqs.e: It describes the Mauryan administration.

mcqs.q: According to Megasthenes, Indian society was divided into how many classes?
mcqs.e: Philosophers, farmers, soldiers, herdsmen, artisans, overseers and councillors.

mcqs.q: Seleucus Nicator was the founder of which dynasty?
mcqs.e: Chandragupta defeated him and, by tradition, married his daughter (Helena).

mcqs.q: Which religion did Chandragupta Maurya adopt at the end of his life?
mcqs.e: He embraced Jainism under the influence of Bhadrabahu.

mcqs.q: What was Ashoka's relationship to Bindusara?
mcqs.e: Bindusara was the son of Chandragupta Maurya.

mcqs.q: Which sect did Bindusara follow?
mcqs.e: The Ajivika sect was founded by Makkhali Gosala.

mcqs.q: Who founded the Ajivika sect?
mcqs.e: It believed in strict determinism (niyati).

mcqs.q: During Bindusara's reign, Ashoka served as viceroy of which region?
mcqs.e: He was also sent to Taxila to suppress a revolt.

mcqs.q: What was the capital of the Uttarapatha province in the Mauryan period?
mcqs.e: Ujjain was the capital of the western province (Avanti).

mcqs.q: What was the capital of the Kalinga province in the Mauryan period?
mcqs.e: Pataliputra was the capital of the eastern/central province.

mcqs.q: What was the capital of Dakshinapatha in the Mauryan period?
mcqs.e: The provinces were governed by princes under central control.

mcqs.q: Who succeeded Ashoka on the Mauryan throne?
mcqs.e: Dasharatha was Ashoka's grandson.

mcqs.q: Who was the last Mauryan ruler?
mcqs.e: Pushyamitra Shunga killed him and founded the Shunga dynasty.

mcqs.q: Which dynasty did Pushyamitra found?
mcqs.e: He assassinated Brihadratha.

mcqs.q: Which Mauryan rulers got the Barabar and Nagarjuni caves excavated for the Ajivikas?
mcqs.e: Barabar caves (Ashoka) and Nagarjuni caves (Dasharatha) are in Jehanabad, Bihar.

mcqs.q: Who got the Nagarjuni caves excavated?
mcqs.e: They are near Jehanabad in Bihar.

mcqs.q: Which text guided the centralised bureaucracy of the Mauryan period?
mcqs.e: It was a feature of Chandragupta's administration.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the elements in Kautilya's Saptanga theory?
mcqs.e: Saptanga: Swami, Amatya, Janapada, Durga, Kosha, Danda, Mitra.

mcqs.q: In the Saptanga theory, what does 'Durga' mean?
mcqs.e: Danda = army, Kosha = treasury, Janapada = territory, Amatya = minister.

mcqs.q: Who was the superintendent of agriculture in the Mauryan administration?
mcqs.e: Sita refers to crown land under cultivation.

mcqs.q: Who was the Akshapataladhyaksha?
mcqs.e: He can also be described as the chief audit officer.

mcqs.q: What was the function of the Samaharta?
mcqs.e: The Samaharta was the Collector-General of revenue.

mcqs.q: Who was the chief treasury officer in the Mauryan period?
mcqs.e: The Sannidhata was the head of the treasury.

mcqs.q: Who was the chief officer of city administration described in the Arthashastra?
mcqs.e: The Gopa was responsible for accounts.

mcqs.q: Who was the superintendent of ships (boats) in the Mauryan period?
mcqs.e: The Ashvadhyaksha was the superintendent of horses (cavalry).

mcqs.q: Who was the superintendent of customs/tolls in the Mauryan period?
mcqs.e: Shulka means toll or duty.

mcqs.q: Which officer supervised the markets in the Mauryan period?
mcqs.e: The Samsthadhyaksha managed the markets.

mcqs.q: What was the village headman called in north India during the Mauryan period?
mcqs.e: The Gramika was the village headman.

mcqs.q: In the Mauryan period, which tax was paid in cash (literally 'gold')?
mcqs.e: Hiranya was a tax paid in cash rather than in kind.

mcqs.q: What was the emergency tax called in the Mauryan period?
mcqs.e: Pranaya was an emergency tax.

mcqs.q: What was 'Senabhaktam' in the Mauryan period?
o: An army-related tax (levied when the army passed through)
mcqs.e: Parshvika was an additional levy, like a surcharge.

mcqs.q: Who were the 'Rajukas' in Mauryan administration?
o: Rural officers in charge of land measurement and justice
mcqs.e: Rajukas were administrative officers in rural areas.

mcqs.q: What was the function of the 'Yukta' in the Mauryan period?
mcqs.e: Yuktas were subordinate officers handling revenue records.

mcqs.q: Which of the following was a major eastern port of the Mauryan period?
mcqs.e: Bharuch (Gujarat) and Sopara (Maharashtra) were western ports.

mcqs.q: According to the Arthashastra, which two types of courts settled disputes?
mcqs.e: Dharmasthiya courts handled civil cases; Kantakashodhana courts, presided over by Pradeshtas, handled criminal cases.

mcqs.q: Who presided over the Dharmasthiya court?
mcqs.e: Kantakashodhana courts dealt with disputes between the state and individuals.

mcqs.q: Which metal was most widely used for coins in the Mauryan Empire?
mcqs.e: These were called punch-marked coins.

mcqs.q: What were punch-marked coins also called?
mcqs.e: They began in the Mahajanapada period.

mcqs.q: After which war did Ashoka embrace Buddhism?
mcqs.e: The war was fought around 261 BC.

mcqs.q: How many years after his coronation was the Kalinga War fought?
mcqs.e: Ashoka's coronation is believed to have taken place four years after his accession.

mcqs.q: Who initiated Ashoka into Buddhism?
mcqs.e: According to the northern Buddhist tradition, Upagupta initiated Ashoka.

mcqs.q: What policy did Ashoka adopt after the Kalinga War?
mcqs.e: Conquest was now by Dhamma, not by war.

mcqs.q: What was the name of Ashoka's elder brother whom he displaced to gain the throne?
mcqs.e: Bindusara wanted Susima to be his successor.

mcqs.q: Which Rock Edict records Ashoka's remorse over the Kalinga War?
mcqs.e: It also describes the Kalinga War.

mcqs.q: How many Major Rock Edicts and Pillar Edicts of Ashoka are there?
mcqs.e: Seven refers to the number of pillar edicts, not the number of pillars.

mcqs.q: What was prohibited in Ashoka's First Rock Edict?
mcqs.e: The Fourth Rock Edict gives priority to Dhammaghosha.

mcqs.q: Which Rock Edict of Ashoka conveys the message of tolerance towards all religions?
mcqs.e: The Twelfth Rock Edict calls for respect for all sects.

mcqs.q: What is the main meaning of 'Dhamma' in Ashoka's inscriptions?
mcqs.e: Dhamma refers to moral rules of conduct.

mcqs.q: Which special officers did Ashoka appoint to propagate Dhamma?
mcqs.e: Dhamma Mahamattas were appointed in the 13th year of his reign.

mcqs.q: Whom did Ashoka send as Buddhist missionaries to Sri Lanka?
o: His son Mahendra and daughter Sanghamitra
mcqs.e: Theravada Buddhism is prevalent in Sri Lanka today.

mcqs.q: In which language are the inscriptions of Ashoka and Kharavela mainly written?
mcqs.e: Prakrit is the most common language of Ashoka's inscriptions.

mcqs.q: How many languages and scripts are found in Ashoka's inscriptions?
mcqs.e: Languages: Prakrit, Greek, Aramaic; scripts: Brahmi, Kharosthi, Greek, Aramaic.

mcqs.q: Which script is most used in Ashoka's inscriptions in north India?
mcqs.e: The pillar edicts are in Prakrit language and Brahmi script.

mcqs.q: Which script was used in Ashoka's inscriptions in the north-west (Peshawar region)?
mcqs.e: Greek and Aramaic were used in Afghanistan.

mcqs.q: Who first deciphered Ashoka's Brahmi inscriptions?
mcqs.e: This was achieved in 1837.

mcqs.q: In which year did James Prinsep decipher the Brahmi script?
mcqs.e: Prinsep identified Ashoka as 'Devanampiya Piyadasi'.

mcqs.q: By which title is Ashoka addressed in his inscriptions?
mcqs.e: It means 'Beloved of the Gods'.

mcqs.q: In which inscription is Ashoka's name clearly mentioned as 'Ashoka'?
mcqs.e: Besides Maski, the name appears at Gujarra (MP), Nittur and Udegolam.

mcqs.q: Who discovered the Maski inscription?
mcqs.e: C. Beadon discovered it in 1915.

mcqs.q: Which material was mainly used for Ashoka's pillars?
mcqs.e: Chunar sandstone was used.

mcqs.q: What is the animal figure at the top of a pillar called?
mcqs.e: Parts of the pillar: shaft, inverted lotus, abacus, capital.

mcqs.q: In which direction do the four lions of the Sarnath Lion Capital face?
mcqs.e: It is the National Emblem of India.

mcqs.q: Which animals are carved between the wheels on the abacus of the Sarnath Lion Capital?
mcqs.e: The abacus shows an elephant, a bull, a horse and a lion separated by wheels.

mcqs.q: Which Ashokan pillar capital is kept in Rashtrapati Bhavan?
mcqs.e: Rampurva is in Bihar.

o: It has four lions on top

mcqs.e: It is located in Bihar.

mcqs.q: In which country is the Nigali Sagar inscription and what does it record?
o: Nepal; enlargement of the stupa of Kanakamuni Buddha
mcqs.e: The Rummindei inscription at Lumbini records a tax remission.

mcqs.q: Which inscription shows that Ashoka granted tax relief to Lumbini?
mcqs.e: The village's tax share was reduced to one-eighth.

mcqs.q: In which period were the stupas of Sanchi and Sarnath originally built?
mcqs.e: These stupas reflect the architecture of Ashoka's time.

mcqs.q: In which present-day state is Sopara, a western port of the Mauryan period?
mcqs.e: Bharuch is in Gujarat.
